question.problem: The total time until a computer component registers an error varies continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of once every $30$ days. Determine the probability that a component will register its next error within the next $2$ to $12$ days. Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Since the errors occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next error using an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $X$ be the time until the next error. The time until the next error can be modeled as an exponential random variable. Since errors occur once every $30$ days on average, the rate is $\lambda =1/30,$ and we can write 

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{30}).
$$

 In this case, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{30}{e}^{-x/30}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that first error will be registered between $2$ and $12$ days is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X<12) & ={\int }_{2}^{12}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{12}\frac{1}{30}{e}^{-x/30}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x/30}{|}_{2}^{12} \\  & =-{e}^{-2/5}+{e}^{-1/15} \\  & ≈0.2652\end{aligned}
$$
